intro.h2: One owner, one written scope, every room
paragraphs: Alpha General Construction offers bathroom remodeling in Midland, TX, along with kitchens and whole-home renovations. Owner Joel Gomez manages each project himself, from reviewing the property and writing the scope to coordinating trades and walking the finished work with you.

Joel also writes Alpha's Behind the Build advice column, and his message is steady: compare the details, not just the total. Your written scope spells out the work, the selections and who is responsible for what, so the price you approve matches the job you get. One wet-room client noted that Alpha gave the highest quote, but it was worth it.

about.h2: Meet Joel Gomez, owner and project manager
about.text: Joel Gomez owns Alpha General Construction and manages its projects personally. He reviews each property, writes the scope, coordinates the trades, talks through selections and stays involved through the final walkthrough. Under his full name, Joel Gomez Rivas, he writes Alpha's Behind the Build articles on comparing bids, planning a kitchen and the questions to ask before a shower demo. Alpha leans on trusted local partners, including Yates Flooring Center for tile and Ferguson for plumbing fixtures, so orders arrive right the first time. Reviewers describe Joel as nice, patient and good at keeping them informed.

image.alt: Joel Gomez, owner and project manager of Alpha General Construction in Midland, TX

process.h2: The Alpha approach in four steps

steps.title: A conversation
steps.text: Book a time online or call. You talk through your home, your priorities and what you want to change, with a rough budget and photos if you have them.

steps.title: A defined scope
steps.text: Existing conditions, selections, responsibilities and budget are worked out and written down, so you know what is included before work begins.

steps.title: A coordinated build
steps.text: Trades, materials, schedules and any changes are managed as one project, with Joel coordinating each phase and keeping you updated.

steps.title: A final walkthrough
steps.text: You and Joel review the agreed work together, and any completion items are addressed before the project is closed out.

faq.h2: Questions to ask Alpha before you remodel

items.q: Can you turn my tub and shower into a wet room?
items.a: Yes. Alpha has converted a shower and tub area into a true wet room with a zero-curb entry. That work involved demolition, framing changes, slab work for the curbless entry, drain relocation, waterproofing, tile, plumbing, electrical, drywall and paint. Curbless designs need this planning up front, so it goes into your written scope.

items.q: How do you keep a new shower from leaking?
items.a: Alpha builds the shower pan to code and flood-tests it, then applies one continuous surface waterproofing system, such as RedGard, to the walls, niche, bench and curb. Tile is set with lasers and long levels. The waterproofing is documented, and the work is backed by a written labor warranty.

items.q: How should I compare remodeling bids?
items.a: Look past the total. A useful proposal states what is included and excluded, who supplies materials, how waterproofing will be done, how hidden conditions are handled and what warranty backs the work. The lowest bid can leave out steps that come back later as change orders.

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel cost in Midland?
items.a: Alpha's kitchen planning guide gives these ranges: semi-custom cabinets about $12,000 to $25,000 or more, custom from about $30,000, and quartz, granite or quartzite at $50 to $100 or more per square foot installed. Set aside 10 to 15 percent for surprises. A full kitchen typically takes 6 to 10 weeks.

items.q: Can I finance a larger renovation?
items.a: You can talk with PrimeLending loan originator Stephanie Hecke about renovation loan programs, where costs may be included in a purchase or refinance mortgage depending on the program. Alpha prepares the construction estimate and project details the lender asks for. PrimeLending makes all credit decisions, and Alpha does not.
